thread:
jordan-cust: Hi support, our private deployment started throwing TLS handshake failures to Redwood hosted API from our app subnet ~10:15 PDT. Calls intermittently get ECONNRESET / curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer. Only from our VPC, public infra works fine. svc endpoint: us-west.inference.redwood.com

alice-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro curl and any tcpdump/traceroute you have? Also confirm if traffic goes via NAT gateway or direct IGW?

jordan-cust: Using NAT gateway. Repro I ran from app pod host: `curl -v https://us-west.inference.redwood.com/v1/health` yields:
```
* Connected to us-west.inference.redwood.com (34.216.1.2) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake has read 0, written 3000
* curl: (35) SSL connect error
* Closing connection 0
```
and client side logs show `socket error: ECONNRESET` in our HTTP client.

sam-eng-infra: This looks like a classic NACL vs SG mismatch. Quick checklist: SGs are stateful so once outbound 443 allowed, return is fine. NACLs are stateless — you must explicitly allow the ephemeral return ports on ingress.

maria-sre: Can you share `tcpdump -n -s0 -w - 'tcp and host 34.216.1.2 and port 443'` output or at least `tcpdump -n -c 20 tcp and host 34.216.1.2 and port 443` lines? That usually tells whether SYN-ACK is coming back.

jordan-cust: Attached sample tcpdump excerpt:
```
15:10:02.123456 IP 10.0.3.12.52137 > 34.216.1.2.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
15:10:02.223789 IP 10.0.3.12.52137 > 34.216.1.2.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [...], length 0
15:10:02.324001 IP 10.0.3.12.52137 > 34.216.1.2.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
```
No SYN-ACKs seen.

alice-support: That strongly suggests the SYN leaves your subnet but the reply isn't making it back to your instance. For NAT setups: ensure your subnet's NACL ingress allows destination port range that includes the ephemeral port (source port of outgoing flow). Commonly people lock down ingress to 443/80 only which blocks return traffic.

sam-eng-infra: Exactly. For clarity: when your host opens `src=10.0.3.12:52137 -> dst=34.216.1.2:443` the reply from Redwood is `src=34.216.1.2:443 -> dst=10.0.3.12:52137`. NACL ingress rules operate on the destination port (here 52137). If you only allowed ingress port 443, you'll drop those packets. NACLs are stateless — you need symmetric rules for egress+ingress.

netbot: Recommended quick NACL rules:
```
# EGRESS (allow out to Redwood)
Type: TCP, PortRange: 443, Dest: 0.0.0.0/0, ALLOW
# INGRESS (allow return ephemeral ports)
Type: TCP, PortRange: 1024-65535, Src: 0.0.0.0/0, ALLOW
```

natalie-support: Also check ephemeral port range on your OS (some use 32768-61000). If you want tighter rules, scope ingress to your NAT public IP / Redwood IPs, but don't forget to include full ephemeral range used by your hosts.

maria-sre: Quick diagnostic commands you can run: `nc -vz us-west.inference.redwood.com 443` (should report open), `traceroute -T -p 443 us-west.inference.redwood.com` to see where packets drop, and `sudo tcpdump -n 'dst host 10.0.3.12 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0'` to watch replies.

jordan-cust: Ok we added a temporary ingress NACL rule (1024-65535 allow from 34.216.0.0/16) and left SGs as-is. Retested and curl now returns 200 on /v1/health. Logs show TLS handshake success.

alice-support: Awesome — can you confirm for us which exact rule you added (rule number + subnet) so we can record for the ticket? Also we'll include mitigation docs.

jordan-cust: Added NACL rule 110 allow ingress TCP 1024-65535 from 34.216.0.0/16 to subnet-0a1b2c, timestamp 15:22. Confirmed across three hosts.

sam-eng-infra: Followups:
- If you want network-level least privilege, limit source to Redwood IPs (we publish IP ranges) or to your NAT's elastic IP.
- If you control the NAT, you can also add a dynamic rule set to only allow Return traffic to your ephemeral port range for the NAT IP.
- If you ever see SYN then immediate RST from our side (tcpdump shows RST from 34.216.1.2), open a ticket and include pcap — that indicates an upstream reset not a NACL drop.

alice-support: We're going to mark this resolved for now since adding the ingress ephemeral rule fixed it. We'll attach this thread + recommended NACL example to the KB: "Private VPC -> Redwood API TLS handshake fails (NACL stateless return ports)". Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

jordan-cust: Thanks all, saved our production job. Closing ticket #SUP-9821.

maria-sre: Adding a quick snippet for the KB: `aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-xxxxx --rule-number 110 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress false --cidr-block 34.216.0.0/16 --rule-action allow`

alice-support: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and share before we publish KB. If anyone sees similar, ping me.
